rounds.critic: Independent RC4 critic for Elf, Orc and Saurian buildings

models.observations: A separate tall tower adjoins a hipped civic hall and deep pillared portico. The sharp span between portico columns and asymmetrical height remain visible in both grey views among all ten Town Center ages, including the neighboring Medieval and Industrial versions. Painted previews cover renaissance. I compared both 64 px unpainted family views and the 215°, 125° and 35° painted middle LOD. Serialized LODs 1247/653/305 passed validation and the 60% ceiling. Direct surface and winding checks found zero exposed coplanar overlaps and zero inverted closed shells. The largest directed corner share involving this model and any sibling was 0.0%.

rounds.critic: RC6 independent housing, town center and Saurian civic critic
rounds.inspection: Compared all sibling entries at 64 px in paint and in both unpainted cameras. Inspected every changed age preview, all three serialized LODs, and reverse views of the middle model. Compared the same-age house alternatives side by side and examined the three races together. Recomputed the picture and directional corner metrics, verified the package metadata and GLB statistics, and checked the actual serialized surfaces and shell orientations for each changed model.

models.observations: The long covered back gallery and side terraces frame a sunken public forecourt. A freestanding disk marks its center. The shape and circulation of the court persist in all LODs and from the reverse view.

At the native scale the single green gable, raised timber deck and straight stair repeat the Saurian Iron v0 house. The wider steps, raised disks, roof pegs and rail differentiate details while the outline still signals a residence.
defects: Rework the primary civic volumes and gathering space. The Town Center needs a plan recognizably different from the Iron stilt house in both grey corners and all three LODs.

models.observations: The stone-footed tower joins one green-gabled entry shed. Beside the Saurian Medieval v0 house the same tall block and short vestibule dominate both corners. A different cap and wider door give the civic building too little independent identity.
defects: Give the Medieval Town Center a distinct public plan and roof break. A larger domestic porch on the side of the same tower does not distinguish its function at 64 px.

models.observations: A tall blue crystal blade stands behind a stepped cylindrical civic chamber. The sloping blade rises clear of the pale disks at every LOD and reads from behind. The Modern cross-winged offices are substantially lower and broader.

A circular blue-banded hub spans three pale radial wings around the entrance stair. The open spaces between wings mark the plan from above and remain at the final LOD. The bronze-and-blue civic crest gives the front a focal point up close.

A brick clock tower stands beside the curved hall roof. The long dark green porch rests on a row of supports facing its civic steps. The tower, vaulted roof and columned approach survive both reductions.

rounds.critic: RC6 independent housing and Saurian civic critic, corrected candidate review
rounds.inspection: Compared the published painted age previews and family sheets against the original holds and named lookalikes. Rendered both unpainted 64 px views independently from each of the three actual LOD meshes. Inspected the native family cameras and the larger multi-camera LOD sheet. Recomputed same-family picture likeness and directional corner overlap, checked the fragment against the GLB and verified all three serialized levels for exposed coplanar faces and inverted shells.

models.observations: Concentric seating tiers gather around a dais inside a circular wall with a broad public entrance. At the rear, a two-post standard rises above the rim. The complete seating bowl survives all LODs and has an immediately different footprint from the Iron stilt house.

A broad open-sided civic pavilion sits on a raised stone terrace reached by a lateral stair. The stair, columned upper pavilion and paired rooftop caps retain the same proportions through reduction. The Medieval house instead places a small side entrance beside its tall, closed residential tower.

rounds.critic: RC6 independent housing and Saurian civic critic, final gallery review
rounds.inspection: Inspected final painted family and package PNGs and each published age preview. Independently rendered both unpainted 64 px camera angles at all three LODs. Verified the live GLB, recomputed the two comparison metrics and checked the three serialized meshes for exposed coplanar faces and inverted shells. Compared the third Iron candidate with the Classical Arena, Iron residence, Bronze and Medieval Town Centers and Classical Forum. Reopened the archived second submission for comparison.

models.observations: A raised longitudinal council hall stands behind an independent gateway, paired terraces and a broad approach stair. Its open-sided nave has a raised ridge cap and a rectilinear floor plan at all three LODs. Both grey corners distinguish it from the Classical Arena’s concentric stands and the Iron residence’s exposed piles. The side terraces and gated public apron also separate it from the later single-pavilion Medieval center.
